Maintenance Report — MNT-0056-005

Asset: WELL-0056 (SW-24 Well 056, T350, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 02 Jun 2023 08:00 · Finished: 02 Jun 2023 20:00 · Well stopped for this job: 12 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0056-0031 on 2023-06-01 Report written: 03 Jun 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0056-0031 at 10:00 on 2023-06-01 found crude oil on the pad: about 9.4% of the pad area, estimated 5.5 bbl. The inspector noted: "Oil sheen around cellar." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 3.6 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to the flanged flowline connection at the wellhead cellar.

Root cause

A failed gasket on the flange where the flowline leaves the wellhead.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 4 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Cleaned free oil out of the cellar.
  2. Unbolted the flange and removed the failed gasket.
  3. Fitted a new gasket and new bolts, torqued to specification.
  4. Excavated the stained soil around the cellar.

Summary of the fix: replaced the flange gasket and bolts and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 329 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 263 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 3.3 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0056-005 (WS-06).
  • 4 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.44% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0056-007

Asset: WELL-0056 (SW-24 Well 056, T350, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 21 Jul 2023 08:00 · Finished: 25 Jul 2023 02:00 · Well stopped for this job: 90 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0056-0038 on 2023-07-20 Report written: 26 Jul 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that oil was dripping from the gearbox onto the pump jack base. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0056-0038 showed the wellhead at 42.4 °C with the air at 39.4 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 2 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

A hardened output shaft seal after years of service.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Used gear oil and oily pads sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0056-007 (WS-06).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0056-016

Asset: WELL-0056 (SW-24 Well 056, T350, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 25 Aug 2024 08:00 · Finished: 04 Sep 2024 11:00 · Well stopped for this job: 243 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0056-0094 on 2024-08-22 Report written: 06 Sep 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running rough with a loud knock at the top of each stroke, so the operator stopped it. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0056-0094 showed the wellhead at 38.4 °C with the air at 35.3 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 8 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0056-021

Asset: WELL-0056 (SW-24 Well 056, T350, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 28 Mar 2025 08:00 · Finished: 09 Apr 2025 17:00 · Well stopped for this job: 297 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0056-0125 on 2025-03-27 Report written: 10 Apr 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the wellhead was cold and the pump jack was straining with a heavy, uneven load. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0056-0125 showed the wellhead at 23.5 °C with the air at 20.2 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. The company workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 10 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

A worn plunger that let sand settle and lock the pump.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0056-023

Asset: WELL-0056 (SW-24 Well 056, T350, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: rod string Work started: 10 May 2025 08:00 · Finished: 13 May 2025 10:00 · Well stopped for this job: 74 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Brian Coleman, Megan Ward · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0056-0131 on 2025-05-08 Report written: 19 May 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running but the wellhead was cold and the rod load had dropped. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0056-0131 showed the wellhead at 37.3 °C with the air at 26.3 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A dynamometer card showed no load from the downhole pump, which points to a parted rod. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 1 day for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

Fatigue failure of a rod body, probably started by corrosion pitting.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 4 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rod string and located the break.
  3. Recovered the lower section with an overshot fishing tool.
  4. Replaced the damaged rods.
  5. Ran the rod string back in and spaced out the pump.

Summary of the fix: fished and replaced parted rod section.

Testing and return to service

Pump test showed normal fluid delivery and the rod load returned to normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

ItemUSD

Rod couplings1,642
Fishing tool rental2,736
Labour (company crew and contractor)6,518
Total17,462

Compliance check

Notes and recommendations

  • Consider corrosion inhibitor treatment for this well.
  • Keep the recovered rod for failure analysis.
  • HSE to follow up on the WS-07 item above with the crew.
